name: Artificial Intelligence
definition: Artificial intelligence is the use of statistical models and computing systems to perform tasks that traditionally required human judgment, including perception, language, reasoning, and generation.
happening: The industry is moving from model capability races into an infrastructure and distribution cycle. Capital expenditure is concentrating among a small group of platforms while enterprises test whether software agents can turn inference into durable productivity.
why: AI sits at the intersection of semiconductor demand, cloud economics, labor substitution, and national industrial policy. The first-order story is compute; the second-order story is who captures the value after models become abundant.
risk: The core risk is a mismatch between infrastructure commitments and monetized demand. Slower adoption, lower inference prices, or power constraints could compress returns before the new capacity earns out.

timeline.event: Inference economics become the new battleground
